conventions.convention: The mirror is the image under a fixed orientation-reversing involution of S3 preserving the standard unknot. Crossing interchange and planar reflection are alternative operations.
The normal-boundary class Yp is the W1,p closure of smooth forms on the closed ball with zero normal component; the Hodge estimate assumes full AC and 2 ≤ p < infinity.
The Neumann inverse solves -Δu=f, has zero volume mean, and satisfies the weak identity against every W1,2 test. Its normalized polynomial-closure domain has norm equivalent to the Lp norm of Δu.

Inst anon constructions assume full AC. The rational closure group uses the generalized surface-zero eigenspace intersected with the ordinary point-plus-two eigenspace; the cited extreme-surface identity identifies it with the ordinary simultaneous eigenspace.

Finite trajectory energy means twice the integral of the squared temporal derivative, rather than unrenormalized curvature energy over an infinite cylinder. The singular complex has relative grading modulo four and a degree-one cochain differential.
The canonical class is an invariant isomorphism class, not a distinguished vector; continuation retains the declared orientation-sign ambiguity.
Reduced Khovanov cohomology uses the quotient by the image of the basepoint X action, with reduced quantum shift j−1 and unknot bidegree (0,0).

The integral resolution spectral sequence has E2 equal to reduced Khovanov cohomology of the mirror; intermediate-page knot invariance is not asserted. Convergence means the associated graded of a finite filtration on instanton homology.

load_bearing.statement: Assume full AC and fix a smooth based knot with the prescribed earring and admissible singular bundle data. Regular perturbation data define a finite free integral cochain complex with square-zero differential; its homology is independent of regular metric and perturbation up to the declared sign and invariant under isotopy of the based data.

Under full AC, the singular instanton resolution complex of a finite based ordered knot diagram has a finite filtration whose first-page complex is the reduced integral Khovanov cube of the reflected diagram, with the stated cube signs and merge/split operations, and converges to integral singular instanton homology.

Assume full AC. For every smooth knot K in S3, KHI(K;Q) is finite-dimensional of dimension at least one, with dimension one exactly for the unknot. Moreover, excision gives I-natural(K;Q) isomorphic to KHI(K;Q).

Assume full AC. Every smooth knot has a finite spectral sequence of abelian groups with E2 the integral reduced Khovanov cohomology of its mirror, bigrading forgotten, converging to its integral singular instanton homology.

Under full AC, for 2 ≤ p < infinity and a in the stated normal approximation class, r−1 times its Lp norm plus its gradient norm is bounded by a radius-independent constant times its exterior derivative and codifferential norms. For Coulomb su(2) forms and 2 ≤ p < 4, sufficiently small L4 norm permits curvature absorption.

Assume full AC. For every finite p ≥ 2, mean-zero Lp data on a four-ball have a unique mean-zero W2,p weak Neumann solution, with the stated scale-invariant estimate and polynomial zero-normal approximation; prescribed finite orthogonal equivariance is preserved.

Under full AC, a smooth su(2) connection on a closed Euclidean four-ball with sufficiently small L2 curvature admits a Coulomb gauge in every finite W2,p, with the stated normal approximation condition and L2/L3 estimates; prescribed finite constant-conjugation equivariance and transformed overlap cocycles are respected.
Assume the Axiom of Choice. The chosen exterior of a smooth nontrivial knot has no properly embedded disk whose boundary is essential on its boundary torus.

concerns.concern: The Definition says that holonomy around either meridian is conjugate to diag(i,−i), immediately after permitting a smooth O(2)-reduced A0 in A0+(1/4)diag(i,−i)dθ. Exact finite-loop holonomy does not follow from that hypothesis. Locally, A0=c diag(i,−i)(x dy−y dx) is smooth and preserves the reduction, but changes radius-r meridional holonomy to exp(±2πi(1/4+cr²)), generally not traceless. Specify limiting meridional holonomy, or impose an appropriate exact model near the link. The primary source explicitly discusses asymptotic holonomy in Proposition 3.2's proof: https://people.math.harvard.edu/~kronheim/khovanov-unknot.pdf, printed p.29.

The braid drawing does not place its undercrossing gaps at the strand intersections. For the upper crossing, the understrand pieces end at (0.10,2.61) and start at (0.10,2.39), while the overstrand is the segment from (−0.45,3) to (0.45,2). The lower understrand fragment actually intersects that overstrand near (0.0994,2.3896), where both strokes are present. The same misplaced geometry repeats at the other two crossings. Thus the picture does not correctly encode the asserted over/under data. The independent cube calculation does not rely on the picture.

The intended quotient norm and completeness assertion remain recognizable, but the statement needs grammatical repair. Batch 97 uses this supplier for completeness only.

seams_checked.note: Exterior, peripheral and homology interfaces support the chosen smooth tubes, preferred-longitude kernel and primitive meridian-longitude basis used here. Full AC discharges the suppliers' countable-choice assumptions.
The reduced quotient, quantum shift, ordered cube signs and based invariance agree. The instanton sequence uses the reflected diagram and forgets the Khovanov bigrading at the stated interface.
Irreducibility uses precisely smooth Schoenflies under countable choice. The disk-to-unknot step uses the genus-zero equivalence with its declared countable-choice assumption.
The JSJ theorem's F2 and Proof 1.1 use smooth exterior irreducibility under full AC, which supplies the cited lemma's countable-choice hypothesis.

The Uhlenbeck consumer invokes the Euclidean small-curvature gauge result for arbitrary smooth local connections. It separately supplies curved-metric regularity and explicitly avoids applying a Euclidean ASD theorem directly to a curved metric.
The complement theorem uses the geometric no-compressing-disk conclusion only after its separate smooth Loop theorem supplies a smooth proper disk from a continuous disk map.

The ordinary and enhanced Newton-edge consumers assume nontrivial knots and full AC before invoking irreducibility and geometric boundary incompressibility. The classification consumer likewise restricts boundary incompressibility to its nontrivial residual branch.
